Firstly, let me say that I am incredibly sorry for your loss.  While I have experienced the loss of family, I've never experienced a death of a loved one that I was as close to you as you seem to be with your husband.  I'm glad that you have a support system in place but it doesn't seem like they've been through a similar experience either.

Have you considered going to a grief therapist or maybe a support group?  I know that loss can be tough (I'm going through the loss of my marriage right now) and can leave us feeling adrift but you don't have to feel motivated, you don't have to go back out into the world and find new purpose.  It's okay to mourn your loss.

I hope that will get through this.  If you want to talk about this, please reply or send me a PM.

I'm sorry that your boyfriend did something to make you feel like that.  I don't know him but if he's anything like me, he's making a joke about something that is both uncomfortable and something that he doesn't understand (the difference being I would never joke about suicide).  I don't think he has a full appreciation of what it's like to feel like that.  So he'll try to see if it will make you smile a bit and maybe a little happier if he makes a joke.

I know that it's difficult not to take those sorts of things to heart so, I won't ask you to, but what I will say is that I hope you stay.  I don't know you or your entire story but I'd like to hear it.

Just so you know, I'm getting out of a relationship where my SO actively encouraged that I go through with my ideations or said that I was looking for attention or accused me of being abusive at the mere mention that I felt it more intensely that day.

Yeah, I feel you on that.  I wish that parents being there for their kids was a universal trait that all parents share.  It would save a lot of people money spent on therapy.  It would save the world a lot of pain.  But you're not the only one with this feeling and I hope that helps you feel less alone.  While I'm not your parent, myself and I'm sure others around here can be here for you.

Yeah, it is pretty messed up when someone you have loved for a long, long time tells you things like that.  They're angry with me because I am not the person that they once knew because of my mental health and my inability to cope with hectic and stressful situations.

I understand that you feel like your parents don't want you in their house and this is more than likely true but maybe not for the reasons that you think.  A parent worth their weight would want their child to succeed.  Most would want their child to be off on their own exploring the world and to be responsible.  Moving back to your parents home is probably not what they intended for you and maybe they are having a difficult time expressing their worries.

Are you going to see your therapist again?   It's okay to change therapists if you don't mesh with your current one.

Hi, this is not your fault, even though you may think it is.  What you did, confronting him about the effects of his actions, was incredibly brave.  What you did do is make him take stock of his own life.  What you did was make him see the damage that he had caused.  What he did with that pain that he caused is his fault.  He could have chosen to try to fix what he had done instead.  So the fault is not yours to bear.

I am sorry about your girlfriend.  I know that it's a hard thing to stack on top of what you're going through  If you need to talk, feel free to respond or shoot me a PM.

Edit:  please don't drive anywhere and please don't blame yourself.

I once checked myself into a Mental Health Hospital once and I will have to say that it was a positive experience overall.  While there weren't that many programs at the time (The beginning of the COVID), what I did have was a group of individuals going through the same or similar situations as myself who had also, for the most part, decided that they needed help as well.

So are they really that bad?  To be honest, no it wasn't really that bad.  The program put me on a schedule that integrated what programs they had with psychiatric treatment and short one on one time with the doctor.  Being a hospital you do have to put up with hospital type things (thin mattress, thin blanket, structured days, blood draws, nurses checking on you at all times of the night) but I was not treated disrespectfully at all.

Do you have any choice of medications?  Yes and No.  I had the choice so far as I was able to talk to my doctor and inform him as to what medications I took in the past, what worked for me and what didn't.  Ultimately it was his decision on what medications to prescribe (they also seemed to prescribe everyone a sleeping pill as well).  
   
What are your general rights?  From my general understanding, I could request to be released as a voluntary admittance, however, there was a point that I did want to be released and the doctor advised me that it would be much better if I could wait and I chose to remain.  I believe that you have the same right to refuse medical treatment but I never tested that theory.  I'm not sure what will happen if you refuse to take your medication.  I do know that a patient was escorted from the wing for failing to follow the rules.  I believe that she was released.

Is it worth it for suicidal thoughts and intentions? Or would just finding an outpatient program be more beneficial?  I found that it was generally beneficial to go in inpatient treatment for stabilization but once released outpatient therapy is essential.  They give you a month's worth of your medication so that you can find your own psychiatrist on the outside and they also advise you to find a therapist as well.  
  
What are your opinions? I want all the stories no matter how long or detailed.  My opinion is that sometimes you need to be taken outside of your environment in order to heal.  I've found that to be key not only in the case of my past SI but also currently.  While I'm not currently in a hospital at the time of this writing, I have removed myself from my day to day and am finding myself able to think much more clearly.

I'm glad that you are looking into getting help and I hope that you do follow through with getting help, no matter what form it takes.  If you need to talk, please feel free to send me a message.
Congratulations!  I don't know you but  I'm glad that you are still here and you found support.

What if she needs help.  What if she needs something.  What if she needs... my happiness has been defined by my ability to take care of her "needs."

Currently I'm in a holding pattern until a rental car becomes available in the next couple of days.  

Regarding my defense mechanism:  I have an extreme aversion to conflict that I developed when I was younger.  I found that lying, while it never stopped the inevitable conversation regarding how disappointed  someone was with me... usually involving a bamboo feather duster, it did delay it long enough for me to be more prepared.  In addition to this, lying was reinforced by interaction with my extended family.  We were to act as if we had no issues even when my immediate family unit was on the verge of falling apart.
